story: Creating a low-cost EV charging station with Arduino
text: In case you don't watch Technology Connections... 1. You probably should, Alec is great. 2. Here's a longer broader video about what goes on in an EVSE: [VIDEO] There are too many comments to go sling context left and right, but generally an EVSE is a controller board (what this is implementing), a contactor (this board uses relays), and a GFCI (in North American parlance), which his RCBO provides along with being a current limiting circuit breaker. Contactors are generally better for these use cases for reliability and current handling reasons but it wouldn't surprise me if SCRs and Relays are in use in low cost 16A EVSEs on Amazon.

story: Bosch gives go-ahead for volume production of silicon carbide chips
text: A quick intro into EVSE and why there is no power 'charger' in them, and the space they take is just empty air [VIDEO]

A helpful video about what's inside an AC EV "charger": [VIDEO] Really the only difference with the fancier ones is they have a screen and payment terminal or NFC terminal for activating and paying. Like a gas pump, although most want you to use their app and membership to save (them) on credit card processing fees. DC fast chargers are a whole different story, where the AC to DC conversion happens external to the car.

story: Electric vehicles close to ‘tipping point’ of mass adoption
text: I'm curious how many EV purchasers live in single family homes, or other places where they can provide their own ability to charge at home. I wonder if a new scale of adoption will require a change where most (or a lot) of street parking is by cheap charging. [VIDEO]
